title: Latency Sentry and Notification Attenuator for Observability Pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a lightweight "sentry" layer and a notification attenuator that sits between tracing/metric ingestion and the alerting layer. The sentry will enrich spans with lightweight health signals, maintain short-term anomaly queues for burst de-duplication, and surface compact signatures to the burn-rate engine. The attenuator will reduce noisy paging by correlating signature clusters, temporary service-level regressions, and synthetic probe context before escalating to on-call. This work covers tracing hooks, metric/log pipeline enrichment, dashboard wiring for latency/error signatures, and new alerting gating logic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sentry shim deployed in staging mode that attaches 'sentry.signature' and 'sentry.score' to enriched spans/metrics. 2) Anomaly queue deduplication reduces equivalent alerts in replay tests by >= 70%. 3) Notification attenuator implements rule engine: cluster correlation + synthetic probe context + SLO burn-rate threshold and only pages when combined score > threshold. 4) Latency/error dashboard shows 'sentry signature' breakdown and time-to-resolution for attenuated vs direct pages. 5) Smoke tests and a-runbook added; no increase in missed-P0 pages over baseline in 2-week canary.
technical_notes: Architecture: small sidecar service (sentry-proxy) deployed in observability ingestion path that computes per-request lightweight embeddings (span signature), canonicalizes attributes, and writes a short TTL queue in Redis/stream for correlation. The attenuator will run as a policy engine in the alert writer stage and consult the queue and synthetic-probe store. Key primitives: span canonicalizer, signature-hash namespace, short-term clustering window (30s-5m), score combiner (burn-rate, probe-corroboration, historical noise), and a fast fallback to direct page for proven P0 signatures. We'll instrument metrics for queue-size, correlation-latency, suppressed_pages, and score-distribution.
risks: 1) Added latency in the ingestion path—mitigate with sampling, fast-path pass-through and circuit-breaker. 2) Over-suppression causing missed pages—mitigate with conservative default thresholds and canary with SLI comparison. 3) Operational complexity of short-term state—keep TTLs short and store compact signatures only. 4) False correlation across tenants—namespace signatures by tenant and service tags.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: prototype sentry-proxy as an optional sidecar reading spans from trace-ingest and posting signatures to Redis stream (2 sprints). Phase 2: implement attenuator policy engine in alert-writer with rule templates and UI flags in Console (1 sprint). Phase 3: staged rollout to non-critical services, collect telemetry and tune thresholds (2 sprints). Phase 4: enterprise rollout with RBAC control for attenuator policy (1 sprint).
test_plan: Unit tests for signature generation and score combiner. Integration tests: synthetic bursts to verify dedupe and suppression ratios. Canary: enable attenuator for a low-traffic namespace for 14 days with automatic rollback if missed page rate rises by >10%. Load test: ensure added latency <5ms median on ingestion path under production-like load with sampling enabled.
updates: 2026-02-25: Spike complete — prototype generates stable 64-bit signature and score. Verified clusterable signatures on replay of last 48h of traces.
2026-03-02: Design review with PM and SRE — agreed on Redis stream TTL=300s and tenant namespacing. Decided to default attenuator to 'observe-only' for first canary.
2026-03-05: Implemented sidecar with pass-through fast-path. Initial integration tests show 3ms median additional latency with 10% sampling.
2026-03-11: Alert-writer policy engine stubbed; UI feature flag added to Console for per-team attenuation toggles. Preparing canary for low-traffic staging cluster next week.
